text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two signs of positive Swedish economic trends appeared on Wednesday. Statistics Sweden said retail sales rose sharply in March, up 2.2 percent from February and up 8.5 percent from March 1996, and mortgage lenders lowered their interest rates
- Swedish consumer prices are expected to rise 1.5 percent over the next 12 months, a May survey by Prospera and commissioned by the central bank, the Riksbank, shows.
- After 17 years as an Electrolux subsidiary, mining group Granges returned to the stock exchange on Wednesday. The share closed at 98 crowns.
- Swedish Junior Labour Minister Ulrika Messing sees a 35 hour work week in 10 years time. Currently, Swedes generally work 40 hours a week.
- Banks are advancing on the pension plan market, taking market share from insurers thanks to their branch offices which give them an extensive distribution network.
- A total of 75 companies have been approved by the Finance Inspectorate so far this year and will list their shares.
- Swedish retail sales rose to their highest level in nearly five years in March. Turnover in retail stores increased by 2.2 percent in March, compared to the previous month, Statistics Sweden said.
- Postgirot, the Swedish post office's check service, plans to reduce its total workforce of 2,400 by 17 percent.
- Financial analysts in Sweden feel that S-E-Banken is heading for big changes, despite repeated denials by the bank's top management.
